# Synthetic scoring baseline

`scoring_base.json` was generated by executing the original `risk_scoring.py`,
`data_quality.py`, and `sensitivity_analysis.py` at commit
`bb6f0b5f7955c09b36db66202e77d29ed3c7d9ad`, not by executing PR #2's scoring code.
It contains no real county observations or personal data.

The fixture records five synthetic counties in three cases: socioeconomic-only,
all numeric input fields populated, and mixed missing fields/values including a
zero population denominator. Integer inputs use NumPy `default_rng(4271)`;
population and socioeconomic fields are specified in the saved inputs.

Each case freezes 374 non-quality output columns, all ten weighting scenarios,
and rank-stability results. Coverage flags, confidence, and quality notes are
intentionally excluded because those are the purpose of this PR. Tests also
compare the non-quality projections of all nine emitted county score tables.

Values were serialized with 15 decimal places; parity tolerance is 1e-12.
Do not update expected values from the candidate implementation merely to make
a failing parity test pass. Revisit the pinned baseline and scope instead.

To reproduce the fixture with the pinned base commit available locally:

```text
python tests/fixtures/generate_baseline.py
```

The generator executes only the pinned baseline modules, redirects their output
files to a temporary directory, and writes this synthetic fixture. It does not
call source APIs or regenerate the project's saved reports or charts.
